prompt_text: Who gets to name the blue comet: the scientist, the student, or the astronaut?
instruction_text:
Conundrums are problems that make you think.

Watch the video carefully. There may not be one perfect answer. Decide what you think, then explain your reasoning. A strong answer tells us what you would choose, why you would choose it, and what might make someone else disagree.

configuration.title: Who Gets to Name the Comet? ☄️
configuration.top_tip: Make a decision first. Then give your strongest reason. Finally, test your idea: What would someone who disagrees with me say?

content_approval.review_scope: Unchanged catalogue title and question, shared introduction and Top Tip template

prompt_text: What was inside my control today, and what was outside my control?
instruction_text:
Reflection is a chance to think carefully about your day.

There is no perfect answer. Choose a real moment, describe what happened, and think about what you can learn from it. Try to focus on your choices, your response, and what you might do next time.

configuration.title: Inside My Control
configuration.top_tip: Separate the two clearly. Then spend most of your writing on what you could choose: your effort, words, attitude, preparation or response.

prompt_text: A dragon arrives at the dentist with a very unusual problem. Unfortunately, the dentist has never treated a dragon before. What happens?
instruction_text:
Silly Stories let your imagination go completely wild.

Use the prompt as your starting point, then take the story anywhere you like. Make something unexpected happen. Your job is not to make the story realistic — it is to make it entertaining while using as many of your Target Words as you naturally can.

configuration.title: The Dragon at the Dentist
configuration.top_tip: Give the dragon a strong personality. Make the problem get worse before somebody finds an unexpected solution.
configuration.category_top_tip:
A fun story usually needs:

Somebody interesting.

Something they want.

A problem that gets in the way.

An unexpected turn.

An ending that changes something.

prompt_text:
You find an old treasure map hidden inside a library book.

Start with: Fortunately, the map showed that the treasure was very close...
instruction_text:
Fortunately / Unfortunately is a story that keeps changing direction.

Begin with the prompt. Then alternate between good news and bad news:

Fortunately... something helpful happens.
Unfortunately... a new problem appears.
Fortunately... things improve again.

Keep switching until you reach an ending.

configuration.title: The Treasure Map
configuration.top_tip: Make each solution create the next problem.
configuration.category_top_tip: Every new sentence should change the situation. Do not simply say something is good or bad — make something actually happen because of it.

prompt_text: Should children have homework after a full day at school?
instruction_text:
Persuasion means trying to convince somebody.

Choose a clear position, then give your strongest reasons. A powerful argument also thinks about what somebody on the other side might say.

You do not have to choose the answer you think an adult would prefer. You need to make the strongest case you can. Write a letter to a headmaster explaining your case. Dear Headmaster, ….

configuration.title: Should Homework Be Banned?
configuration.top_tip: Think about learning, free time, family life and whether all homework is equally useful.
configuration.category_top_tip:
Use this simple structure:

My position: say exactly what you think.

My reasons: give two or three strong reasons.

An example: show why one reason matters.

The other side: mention a reasonable objection.

My reply: explain why you still think your position is stronger.
